subject.title: trusted-proxy auth: support fallback/default user when identity header is absent

question: Should trusted-proxy auth support an explicit fallback/default identity when a request from a trusted proxy source lacks the configured identity header?
rationale: The code change is mechanically bounded, but it changes Gateway auth from requiring per-request identity evidence to accepting proxy-source trust plus a configured principal, which automation should not decide.

options.title: Approve narrow fallback mode
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in single-principal fallback with fail-closed defaults, audit/docs/schema updates, and tests for proxy source, loopback, required headers, origin, and allowlist semantics.

options.title: Keep fail-closed
options.body: Document Cloudflare Zero Trust IP-whitelist/no-identity WebSocket setups as unsupported for trusted-proxy auth and point users to password auth, Tailscale Serve, or a proxy path that forwards identity headers on WebSocket upgrades.

options.title: Require live Cloudflare proof first
options.body: Ask for reproducible Cloudflare Tunnel/WebSocket proof before deciding whether OpenClaw should add a headerless trusted-proxy identity surface.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow fallback mode
recommendation.body: Add an explicit opt-in single-principal fallback with fail-closed defaults, audit/docs/schema updates, and tests for proxy source, loopback, required headers, origin, and allowlist semantics.
